report.summary: Chunk 6 of 6 of killswitch.py: final methods of KillSwitch (stop, clear), _WatchScope context manager, and operator CLI _main.
risks: stop method | medium | Raises LoopHalted even if errors list is empty but state.running is true; the message includes 'no error' but the exception indicates failure. | Check if read_state() after writing can ever return running when both writes succeeded.
clear method | low | Uses os.unlink, which may raise on permission errors; OSError is caught and silently ignored. | Verify that ignoring unlink errors is safe.
_main | low | Parses arguments manually; --force is stripped from note but other flags may be included. | Consider using argparse for robustness.

handoff.purpose: Final chunk: stop, clear methods, _WatchScope context manager, and CLI entry point.

symbols.name: KillSwitch.stop
symbols.note: Writes body to self._marker and self._path, then latches self._tripped, sets event, reads state, and may raise LoopHalted if still running.

symbols.name: KillSwitch.clear
symbols.note: Deletes self._marker and self._path via os.unlink, ignoring OSError.

symbols.name: _WatchScope
symbols.note: Context manager that calls switch.start_watch() on enter and switch.stop_watch() on exit.

symbols.name: _WatchScope.__enter__
symbols.note: Calls self._switch.start_watch() and returns the switch.

symbols.name: _main
symbols.note: CLI entry point: parses args, dispatches to verb (stop, arm, clear, status), returns exit code.

claims.text: Neither write failing is swallowed and neither is allowed to abort a stop that did take: this raises only if, after both attempts, the switch still reads as running.
claims.why: The code attempts both writes, collects errors, then reads state; raises LoopHalted only if state.running is True, regardless of errors. If both writes failed but read_state() returns not running, no exception is raised.

claims.text: An operator's stop command must be loud when it did nothing and quiet when it worked.
claims.why: If stop succeeds (state.running is False), returns normally (quiet). If stop fails (state.running is True), raises LoopHalted (loud).

claims.text: Latch THIS object too. The operator asked this switch to stop; that must not depend on a subsequent read of a disk that just misbehaved.
claims.why: After writing, under lock, sets self._tripped and self._reason regardless of read_state outcome.

claims.text: Remove permit and marker. Leaves the switch STOPPED (no permit).
claims.why: The docstring claims the switch remains STOPPED, but the clear method only deletes files; it does not modify self._tripped. The actual state depends on the object's internal latch, which is not changed by clear. This claim cannot be verified without inspecting read_state or the rest of the class.

observations.what: stop method: errors list is built but only used in the exception message; if state.running is False, errors are silently ignored.
clear method: deletes files but does not reset self._tripped or self._reason; the switch remains logically stopped.
_main: parsing is manual; --path consumes next argument, --force is stripped from note, but other flags may be misinterpreted.
_main: arm verb can raise LoopHalted, caught and printed, returns exit code 4.
